If rail guns use magnetism. Why the flames?

Basic thermodynamics. When fired, the railgun round produces a huge amount of energy from friction with the surrounding air. The fire occurs due to the adiabatic compression of the air. Essentially, the air in and near the "barrel" is compressed so quickly that it cannot displace rapidly, and the round imparts large amounts of energy to it. Since there is work being done to the air, it increases the temperature of the air in the near field of the "barrel" to very high values, which is apparently enough to combust the oxygen gas within the air and thus the flash and flame plume.

The same principle is utilized to create fire via a fire piston.
